description:
We are The Lunar Leftovers.

Our mission is to remember what NASA left behind on the Moon. From Apollo rovers and flags to cameras and footprints, tons of hardware still rests on the lunar surface.

People call it abandoned. We call it abundant history. Our project, Abundant, But Not Forgotten, brings these forgotten artifacts back to life, so the world can see, learn, and preserve what humanity left on the Moon.
summary: Our project, "The Lunar Leftovers," addresses the challenge of forgotten space heritage—specifically the historical hardware, rovers, and landers left behind by NASA and space missions in deep space, on the Moon, and on Mars. As humanity reaches further into the cosmos, the machines that paved the way are left as silent monuments. This project is important because it preserves space history and inspires future generations by breathing life into these abandoned artifacts. Using NASA’s open data and telemetry logs, our solution features an automated story generator and documentary creator. It transforms raw historical data into engaging, emotional narratives and visual documentaries, detailing the journeys, triumphs, and final resting places of these historic space explorations. Through this, we connect people back to the pioneers of space exploration.
details: "The Lunar Leftovers" is a story generator and documentary creation project that brings the history of abandoned space hardware back to life. This includes rovers and landers left behind by NASA and other space missions on the Moon, on Mars, and in deep space. The system uses NASA open data, telemetry logs, and historical mission archives. An automated narrative generator turns them into chronological stories and visual documentary scripts about the journeys and final resting places of these historic machines. Benefits and Intended Impact: The project preserves space history in an engaging story format. Its main impact is educational and inspirational. It connects complex space science with the general public and sparks curiosity about space exploration in young people. Tools and Technologies Used: We used open-access NASA datasets, scriptwriting frameworks, YouTube and Google Drive for hosting video and documents, and Canva for presentation slides, visual assets, and documentary media. Creativity and Team Considerations: We see abandoned space hardware as storytellers of humanity's journey into space, not as space debris. Our team balanced historical accuracy with emotional storytelling, so the content is accessible, engaging, and visually appealing for all ages.
